terms.definition: A disk galaxy with a straight bar of stars across its center and spiral arms winding from the bar's ends — the Milky Way's type.
The distance light travels in one year — about 9.5 trillion kilometers. Used to measure the galaxy's vast scale.
terms.whyItMatters: The Milky Way is 100,000 of them wide.

terms.definition: The flat, spinning plane of the galaxy containing most of its stars, gas, and dust — about 100,000 light-years across.
terms.whereItIs: The visible whirlpool part of the galaxy
terms.whyItMatters: The Sun and most of the night sky's stars live inside it.

terms.definition: A sparse, roughly spherical cloud of old globular clusters and faint stars surrounding the disk.
terms.whereItIs: Wrapping the disk far above and below

terms.definition: The time the Sun takes to complete one orbit of the galaxy — about 230 million Earth-years.
terms.whyItMatters: The Sun has made only ~20 galactic orbits since it formed.
